seat.BEST_WHY: The room floor is the strongest surface in the deck and 1 is the frame that puts nothing wrong on top of it. The blocks run in a broken bond with widths that vary along a row (the row right of the figure at y≈480 has one block about 1.5x the width of its neighbours), each block carries its own scratch-hatch that differs from the next, and a few blocks sit a step darker than the run (the block at roughly (575-665, 455-490)), so the floor reads as laid stone rather than a stamp. Each block has a short dark tick on one side of its joint only, so the blocks read as standing proud of the mortar under a single light direction. The brazier at (580-620, 523-567) throws its own warm pool that overlaps the figure's colder light, and the hatching stays legible through both, so the two sources read as light on stone and not as two overlays. The wall band across the top of the room carries dark driven pins at irregular spacing (around x≈295, 388, 478) which sells the repair fiction without a caption. All four props (crate, pillar, log bundle, brazier) sit on the floor plane and none touches the wall band. The log bundle at (380-513, 593-647) has rope that passes over and under the logs.
seat.WORST_WHY: The pool at (248-343, 0-190) is a hard-edged rectangle of flat teal with a visibly repeating hex-scale pattern, no bank, no shadow, and no transition into the dirt on any side. The grey walkway is a perfectly regular grid: every slab the same size with a single 1px joint, which is a stamp. The moss decal at (12-46, 52-86) is the same shape as the one at (13-43, 207-233). The door at (27-34, 128-149) is taller than the wall face it sits in, so its lower half continues down over the dirt floor as a brown column to y≈167. There is no light falloff anywhere; the tile at the screen corner is the same value as the tile under the figure, which is the one thing the brief says every frame should do. Overall it reads as an asset-pack tileset with a room drawn in it.

panel.ruling: five seats; block only on strong-majority regression (>=4 of 5 rank below the reference); else install if exit met and plant caught. Rank-in-deck cannot resolve polish-sized deltas at a 40% flip rate. — Rafe, 2026-09-09
panel.law: a gate's binding term must have a measured noise floor and must never be a single sample. — Rafe, 2026-09-08

_what: THE ITEM'S OWN MEASURED EXIT — required by INSTALL-LATEST (Rafe, 2026-09-08).
A build installs because it DID THE THING IT SET OUT TO DO. The rank test only says
the doing cost nothing against the seeded reference; this says what was done. Without
it, 'not worse than the reference' would mean 'not different from it', and a round
that changed nothing would install as readily as one that fixed something.
Declared here per item, recorded into the verdict, re-checked at the gate. The gate
refuses a `met` with no measurement behind it.
